instruction: From now on, I always want cubes on the purple zone, cups on the cyan zone and books on the orange zone. Please tidy the table that way.

attempts.code:
import math

obs = observe()
obj = obs["objects"]["red_book"]
zone = obs["zones"]["orange_zone"]

# Calculate grasp height: object top_z minus a small clearance (0.01m)
grasp_h = obj["top_z"] - 0.01

# Calculate yaw: align with long axis of the book
yaw = obj["long_axis_yaw"]

# Pick the object
pick(obj["name"], grasp_h, yaw)

# Move to zone center (dx, dy = 0)
place(zone["name"])

task_spec.refined_instruction: The robot must place the red_book (kind: book) onto the orange_zone and the yellow_cup (kind: cup) onto the cyan_zone. Since both objects are currently not on any defined zone (on_zone: null), the robot should first locate and pick up each object, then move them to their respective target zones. Success is achieved when the red_book is resting on the orange_zone and the yellow_cup is resting on the cyan_zone, with no other objects obstructing these placements.
